title: foldkit-viz plot spec
$comment: Generated by tools/plot-schema.ts from packages/foldkit-viz/src/plot/types.ts. Do not edit by hand.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema this spec follows, for editors and validators: the package's plot-spec.schema.json. compilePlot ignores it.

data.description: Data for every mark without its own `data`: rows, or a column table.

facet.description: Split every mark's rows into small multiples by these fields, on shared scales.

clip.description: Clip marks to each facet's plot area, as a zoomed domain needs. Default false, so dots on the edge of the domain are drawn whole.

projection.description: Draws geo marks, and places dots and text by longitude and latitude, on a map.

coordinates.description: Polar maps x to angle and y to radius, in the largest circle each facet fits.

polar.description: Polar layout: the inner radius as a share of the outer, and where the angle starts, in degrees clockwise from twelve o'clock.

PlotData.description: A plot's or a mark's data: row objects, or a column table.

ColumnTable.description: Data as named columns of equal length, as Polars, DuckDB and Arrow hold it. Build one with `columnTable`, or from an Arrow table with `fromArrow`.

Column.description: One field's values. In JSON, an array; in JavaScript a column may also be a typed array such as Float64Array.

padding.description: Band scales only: share of each step left empty, in [0, 1). Default 0.1.

axis.description: False hides the tick labels and grid, as for tile maps; positions still invert.

PlotValueFormat.description: A portable display format for an axis and the values it describes.

scheme.description: A scheme from math/schemes. Defaults: tableau10, viridis, rdBu.

range.description: Categorical only: explicit colours, in domain order, instead of a scheme.

SchemeName.description: A colour scheme from math/schemes, by name.

range.description: Symbols in domain order. Default: circle, cross, diamond, square, star, triangle, wye.

SymbolScaleSpec.description: Maps a dot mark's symbol field onto symbols.

ProjectionSpec.description: A map projection, fitted to the geo marks in each facet (or the whole sphere). `zoom` scales about `center`, given as longitude and latitude.

symbol.description: A field mapped onto symbols, or a constant such as `{ value: 'square' }`.

dense.description: Compile to one packed `points` graphic instead of a graphic per row, for hundreds of thousands of rows drawn on canvas. Per-row keys and titles are dropped; `indexPlot` names the row under the pointer instead.

highlight.description: Dims rows that do not match. Applies to dot, bar, cell, link and text marks, and to line and area marks a series at a time: a series stays lit when any of its rows matches.

key.description: Field giving each row a stable identity. Default: the row's position.

Channel.description: A field name, or a constant.

Highlight.description: Rows to keep at full opacity; the rest are dimmed. Matching is by a field falling in a range (numbers, or ISO dates as instants) or among values.

z.description: Field splitting rows into series. Default: the stroke field, if any.

transform.description: One transform, or several applied in order, such as a window then a downsample.

highlight.description: Dims rows that do not match. Applies to dot, bar, cell, link and text marks, and to line and area marks a series at a time: a series stays lit when any of its rows matches.

StackOffset.description: How stacked pieces sit: `zero` stacks positive values up and negative values down from zero; `normalize` scales each stack to one; `center` and `wiggle` give streamgraph baselines (areas only).

StackOrder.description: Which series sits nearest the baseline. `input` keeps the order series first appear.

y0.description: Where a vertical bar starts instead of zero, for interval bars such as candle bodies.

x0.description: Where a horizontal bar starts instead of zero.

group.description: Place the series side by side within each band.

BinTransform.description: Bins a rect mark's rows: `x` alone gives a histogram, `x` and `y` a two-dimensional one. Thresholds are a count or, for `x` alone, explicit breaks. Binned rows carry `x1`, `x2` (and `y1`, `y2`), `count` and, for a histogram, `proportion`.

value.description: The reduced value field, such as count or proportion.

PrebinnedRect.description: A rectangle from x1 to x2 and y1 to y2 on continuous axes; a missing x1 or y1 starts at the axis baseline. With a bin transform, `x` (and `y`) are the values to bin and the edges are computed.
